newsitem.title: USA: Dow seen mixed at open, other U.S. stocks seen up.
newsitem.headline: Dow seen mixed at open, other U.S. stocks seen up.

text.p: The Dow industrials were expected to be hampered at the open on Wednesday by a weaker-than-expected quarter from component Eastman Kodak Co, but broader equities markets were expected to rise.
The Dow would be troubled by Kodak's results but a solid second quarter results from giant chipmaker Intel Corp would boost technology stocks and the overall stock market at the start, analysts said.
Bonds and stocks would also take direction from consumer price index and industrial production data, due today.

"The Dow will have problems with Eastman Kodak, which had a disappointing quarter all around," Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker, said. "The Dow will reflect results from Kodak and GM, but the broader market will probably trade higher, at least iniitially, with good results from Intel."
Eastman Kodak reported second quarter earnings of $1.12 per share compared to $1.30 per share in the prior quarter and a First Call consensus estimate of $1.39 per share.

"The Kodak results will impede the Dow but I doubt if it will put a stop to it," Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities said. "If Hewlett-Packard rallies because of Intel, it might offset Kodak."
In pre-opening trade, Kodak was trading at 73, off 3-14/16 points from its closing price.

Another Dow componet, car maker General Motors also posted results, earning $2.68 per share in its second quarter compared to $2.63 per share in the year-ago quarter. The First Call consensus earnings estimate was $2.10 per share.
Better-than-forecast results from Intel, the world's largest producer of microprocessors, were expected to boost Nasdaq, which has been closing at record highs each day.
Intel reported second quarter earnings of $0.92 per share compared to $0.59 per share in last year's second quarter and a First Call consensus estimate of $0.90 per share.
"The tech stocks will be the leaders today, and I suspect we might close above 8,000 on the Dow," Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments said.
Only a strong rise in the consumer price index, due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, could derail markets, analysts said.
The consumer price index was seen up 0.2 percent in June compared to a 0.1 percent rise in May.
The dollar was off its highs against the yen, trading at 115.45/55 yen. In Europe, the dollar was firm, trading at 1.7928/33 marks.
Japan's Nikkei average closed up 289.33 points, or 1.44 percent, at 20,358.74.
In London, the FTSE 100 was up 64.8 at 4964.1.
U.S. stocks trading in London pointed to a higher opening for the Dow, with most activity seen in Intel.

The Wall Street Journal said in its Heard on the Street column that judging by the stock performance of companies which make athletic footwear and apparel, it seems kids are spending more time on the Internet than outdoors.
The New York Times said in its Market Place column that the Brazilian shares fell amid nervous profit-taking and fears about the country's currency.
